claim: Natural-frequency formats aid probability understanding but lose benefit for low-probability high-consequence events like major earthquakes.
stance_target: evidence-based map design improves hazard comprehension
quoted_support: the benefits of using natural frequencies decrease when dealing with low-probability, high-consequence (LPHC) events like major earthquakes, where even significant increases in relative probability remain small in absolute terms.

claim: At L'Aquila 2009, official reassurance led many to remain indoors when the M6.3 quake struck.
stance_target: evidence-based map design improves hazard comprehension
quoted_support: These assurances given by officials led many to remain in their homes when the earthquake struck.
